title: The Lord's Day kept
hook: Scottish Presbyterians kept a quiet, holy Sunday

segments.voice: Yesterday, family worship: a household reading and praying together at the table. Your line was the household at prayer. Who did you read a psalm with? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-two.

It's the first day of the week, in Troas, and the church has gathered in an upstairs room to break bread. Paul is leaving in the morning, so he keeps talking, and talking, until midnight. A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, sinks into a deep sleep and falls from the third loft, and is taken up dead. Paul goes down, embraces him, and says his life is in him. Then he goes back upstairs, breaks bread, and talks until daybreak. That scene from the book of Acts is a glimpse of Christians gathering on the first day. Today is about a tradition that kept that day whole. Today's word: the Lord's Day kept.

The Gospels say the empty tomb was found on the first day of the week. So Christians came to gather on that day, and in Revelation, John writes, "I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day." Scottish Presbyterians, heirs of the Reformed way we've followed this week, took that day and kept all of it. Their Westminster Confession calls it the Christian Sabbath. It asks for rest from ordinary work and from recreations, and the whole day given to worship, in church and at home, with room left for works of necessity and mercy. In homes that kept it this way, the Sunday clothes came out, in some the meal was made the day before, and the hours went to church, the Bible, the catechism, a quiet walk, a visit to someone ill. From outside it could look stern. To those who loved it, it was a day the rest of the week couldn't touch. Behind it sits the old commandment: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy." And Isaiah's picture of people who "call the sabbath a delight." Christians keep the day in different ways. Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday, the seventh day, as the Sabbath. Other Christians hold that in Christ every day belongs to God, and keep Sunday for worship without the full Sabbath rules. Jesus himself said, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." Jewish neighbors keep their own Sabbath on the seventh day. This week walked through prayer said in common, Luther's garland for his barber, an only comfort, psalms in rhyme, a long meditation, a family at the table. It ends with a whole day handed back.

Here's the practice: keep a small sabbath, right now. Put your phone face down, out of reach if you can. Let your shoulders drop. For these two minutes, nothing needs answering, fixing or finishing. If a task floats up, let it wait; it will still be there. If you pray, you can give these minutes to God. If you don't, simply rest in them. And before the bell, choose one hour this Sunday you'll keep quiet. The bell holds the time.
The Lord's Day kept. Sunday, the first day of the week, set apart whole for rest, worship and mercy, the way Scottish Presbyterians kept it.
Your line: a day set apart. Today, put one quiet hour for Sunday on your calendar, and guard it like an appointment. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-two.

howItsDone: Christians gather for worship on Sunday, the Lord's Day. In the Scottish Presbyterian tradition the whole day was kept for church, Bible reading, rest and works of mercy; Seventh-day Adventists keep Saturday as the Sabbath.
